title: The Bashment & Reggae Quiz
subtitle: Fifteen questions. Twenty seconds each. Fastest fingers win.
notes: Written 3 September 2026 for a short two-quiz night. Ska and rocksteady through roots, lovers rock, dancehall and modern bashment, so the room gets more than one era. READ EVERY QUESTION IN THE EDITOR BEFORE THE GIG — these were written in one pass without the generator's second checking call.

rounds.title: Round One — Bashment & Reggae
rounds.blurb: 15 questions on reggae, dancehall and bashment

questions.prompt: Which 1968 Toots and the Maytals song put the word on a record label for the first time?
questions.answerNote: It was spelt "reggay" on the label, and the whole genre took its name from it.

questions.prompt: Which Jamaican singer took "Israelites" to number one in the UK in 1969?
questions.answerNote: Desmond Dekker & the Aces reached the top of the UK chart with it in April 1969.

questions.prompt: Which 1977 Bob Marley and the Wailers album contains "Jamming" and "One Love"?
questions.answerNote: Marley recorded it in London after leaving Jamaica, and Time later called it the album of the century.

questions.prompt: Which British reggae band had a number one with their version of "Red Red Wine"?
questions.answerNote: Neil Diamond wrote it, but the band learned it from Tony Tribe's reggae version.

questions.prompt: Which 2002 Sean Paul album features "Get Busy" and "Gimme the Light"?
questions.answerNote: It won him the Grammy for Best Reggae Album.

questions.prompt: "Pass the Dutchie" was a 1982 UK number one for which young British reggae band?
questions.answerNote: The band were still schoolboys in Birmingham when it went to number one.

questions.prompt: Which Jamaican pair, a drummer and a bass player, are known as the Riddim Twins?
questions.answerNote: Sly Dunbar plays the drums and Robbie Shakespeare played the bass on hundreds of records.

questions.prompt: Which 1972 film starring Jimmy Cliff carried reggae to a far wider audience?
questions.answerNote: Its soundtrack was the first reggae record a lot of people ever owned.

questions.prompt: Which 1982 Gregory Isaacs song shares its name with the album it appeared on?
questions.answerNote: Isaacs was known as the Cool Ruler, and this is the song he is remembered for.

questions.prompt: Which dancehall star was born Adidja Palmer?
questions.answerNote: Mavado led the rival Gully side of dancehall's best-known feud with him.

questions.prompt: Which 2005 Damian Marley album takes its name from his own track "Welcome to Jamrock"?
questions.answerNote: Damian is Bob Marley's youngest son and is nicknamed Jr Gong.

questions.prompt: Which Jamaican singer won the Grammy for Best Reggae Album in 2020 with "Rapture"?
questions.answerNote: Rapture was her debut EP, and she was nineteen when it won.

questions.prompt: Which duo had 1990s hits with "Tease Me" and "Murder She Wrote"?
questions.answerNote: Murder She Wrote is one of the most recycled riddims in all of dancehall.

questions.prompt: Which teenage duo topped the UK chart in 1978 with "Uptown Top Ranking"?
questions.answerNote: They were teenagers from Kingston and it was the only UK hit they ever had.

questions.prompt: Which Lee "Scratch" Perry studio behind his Kingston home shaped the sound of 1970s dub?
questions.answerNote: Perry recorded the Congos and Max Romeo there before the place burned down.
